questions.prompt: How much of our actions does fortune govern, according to Machiavelli?
options: About half; the other half is left to us
questions.explanation: He compares fortune to a flooding river that you can build dikes against in calm times.

questions.prompt: Why did the Italian princes lose their states?
options: Because of their own negligence, not bad luck
questions.explanation: Blaming fortune is the excuse of someone who didn't prepare.

questions.prompt: What does the final chapter call for?
options: For a prince to free Italy from the foreign "barbarians"
For Italy to submit to France
For the Roman Empire to be restored
For the principalities to be dissolved
questions.explanation: The exhortation ends with lines by Petrarch about virtue against fury.

books.title: The Odyssey
books.author: Homer

fieldNotes.humanities: the story so many other stories borrow from

books.synopsis: After ten years of war at Troy and ten more lost at sea, Odysseus fights gods, monsters and a houseful of suitors to get home to Ithaca.

questions.prompt: Who visits Telemachus in disguise in Book 1 and urges him to look for news of his father?
questions.explanation: The goddess appears as Mentes, an old friend of the family, and gives Telemachus courage.

questions.prompt: What trick had Penelope used to put off the suitors?
options: She wove a shroud for Laertes by day and unpicked it by night
She pretended to be ill for three years
She hid in her father's house
She promised to marry the strongest of them
questions.explanation: One of her maids betrayed the trick, as the suitor Antinous complains in Book 2.

questions.prompt: Whom does Telemachus visit to ask about his father?
options: Agamemnon in Mycenae and Priam in Troy
Nestor in Pylos and Menelaus in Sparta
questions.explanation: Menelaus tells him that Odysseus is alive, held on Calypso's island.

questions.prompt: Who orders Calypso to let Odysseus go?
questions.explanation: Athena pleads his case to the gods, and Zeus sends Hermes to the island.

questions.prompt: Who finds Odysseus washed up on the shore of the Phaeacians?
questions.explanation: Athena sends her to the river to wash clothes so that she will meet him.

questions.prompt: What makes Odysseus weep at the Phaeacian court?
options: The sight of a ship from Ithaca
The bard Demodocus singing about the Trojan War
questions.explanation: When the bard sings of the wooden horse, the king notices his tears and asks who he is.

questions.prompt: What name does Odysseus give the Cyclops Polyphemus?
questions.explanation: When the blinded Cyclops shouts that Nobody is hurting him, the other Cyclopes leave him alone.

questions.prompt: How do Odysseus's men lose the bag of winds that Aeolus gave him?
options: They open it near Ithaca, thinking it holds treasure
It is burned in a storm
questions.explanation: The released winds blow the ships all the way back to Aeolus, who refuses to help again.

questions.prompt: How does Odysseus listen to the Sirens and survive?
options: His crew plug their ears with wax and tie him to the mast
Athena makes him deaf for a day
questions.explanation: Circe had warned him; he begs to be untied, and the crew only tie him tighter.

questions.prompt: How does Athena disguise Odysseus when he lands in Ithaca?
questions.explanation: Nobody must recognize him until he can take revenge on the suitors.

questions.prompt: Who gives Odysseus shelter first, without knowing who he is?
questions.explanation: Eumaeus treats the stranger kindly and speaks of his lost master with love.

questions.prompt: Where do Odysseus and Telemachus meet and recognize each other?
questions.explanation: Athena briefly restores Odysseus's true appearance, and father and son weep together.

chapters.title: Books 17–20: The beggar in his own house

questions.prompt: Who is the first to recognize Odysseus when he reaches the palace?
questions.explanation: The neglected dog wags its tail, lowers its ears and dies after twenty years of waiting.

questions.prompt: How does the old nurse Eurycleia recognize him?
options: By the scar on his leg from a boar hunt
questions.explanation: She feels the scar while washing his feet, and he silences her so his plan is not ruined.

chapters.title: Books 21–24: The bow and the bed

questions.prompt: What contest does Penelope set for the suitors?
options: String Odysseus's bow and shoot an arrow through twelve axe heads
A chariot race around the island
questions.explanation: None of the suitors can even string the bow; the beggar does it with ease.

questions.prompt: How does Penelope make sure the stranger really is Odysseus?
options: She asks him to show the scar
She asks for their bed to be moved, and he says it is built around a living olive tree
She asks him the name of their son
questions.explanation: Only he could know the secret of the bed he built himself.

questions.prompt: How does the conflict with the suitors' families end?
options: Athena stops the fighting and imposes peace
questions.explanation: With Zeus's support, the goddess ends the cycle of revenge.

books.title: The Theban Plays
books.author: Sophocles

fieldNotes.law: the law against your conscience
fieldNotes.psychology: Oedipus, and the truth about himself he couldn't see

books.synopsis: Three tragedies about Oedipus and his children, in which knowing the truth, obeying the law and loving your family all come at a terrible price.

questions.prompt: What does the oracle of Apollo say Thebes must do to end the plague?
options: Find and drive out the killer of the old king, Laius
questions.explanation: Oedipus swears to find the murderer, not knowing he is cursing himself.

questions.prompt: Who first tells Oedipus that he is the man he is looking for?
questions.explanation: Oedipus refuses to believe him and accuses him of plotting with Creon.

questions.prompt: What does Oedipus do when he discovers the truth?
options: He blinds himself with the brooches from Jocasta's robe
questions.explanation: Jocasta has hanged herself; Oedipus asks to be cast out of Thebes.

questions.prompt: Where do the old, blind Oedipus and Antigone arrive at the start of the play?
options: At Colonus, near Athens, in the sacred grove of the Furies
questions.explanation: An oracle had told him that he would die and find rest in such a place.

questions.prompt: Who offers Oedipus protection?
questions.explanation: Theseus defends him even when Creon tries to drag him back by force.

questions.prompt: How does Oedipus answer his son Polynices when he asks for his blessing?
options: He curses him and predicts that the brothers will kill each other
He blesses him and gives him his crown
questions.explanation: The curse sets up the tragedy of Antigone.

questions.prompt: Why does Antigone defy King Creon?
options: She wants to take the throne
She buries her brother Polynices, whom Creon ordered to be left unburied
questions.explanation: She puts the unwritten laws of the gods above the decree of the king.

questions.prompt: What punishment does Creon order for Antigone?
options: Death by stoning in the square
To be shut up alive in a rock tomb
To be sold as a slave
questions.explanation: He gives her a little food so that the city is not stained by her death.

questions.prompt: What happens when Creon finally changes his mind?
options: It is too late: Antigone, Haemon and then Creon's wife Eurydice are dead
Antigone is saved and marries Haemon
Teiresias brings Antigone back to life
questions.explanation: Creon is left alive, alone and broken by his own stubbornness.

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius

fieldNotes.psychology: a mind training itself to stay calm
fieldNotes.business: an emperor's private notes on leading well
fieldNotes.humanities: Stoic philosophy in its own words

books.synopsis: The private notebook of a Roman emperor who, between military campaigns, wrote to himself about how to live well, act justly and accept death.

chapters.title: Book 1: What I learned from others

questions.prompt: What is the first book of the Meditations?
options: A list of what he learned from his family, teachers and friends
questions.explanation: He thanks his grandfather, his mother, his teachers and his adoptive father, Antoninus Pius.

questions.prompt: What does he thank his teacher Rusticus for, among other things?
options: Introducing him to the writings of Epictetus
questions.explanation: Rusticus lent him his own copy of Epictetus, the Stoic philosopher who had been a slave.

questions.prompt: What does Marcus tell himself to expect at the start of each day in Book 2?
options: To meet meddling, ungrateful and arrogant people, who cannot really harm him
questions.explanation: Since they share in the same reason, he should not be angry with them but work with them.

questions.prompt: Where, according to Book 4, can a person find the best retreat?
questions.explanation: Nowhere is quieter than one's own soul, and you can withdraw there whenever you like.

questions.prompt: What does Marcus tell himself at dawn when he does not want to get out of bed (Book 5)?
options: That he is getting up to do the work of a human being
That the emperor must set an example for soldiers
That he will rest after the war
questions.explanation: Was he made to lie under the blankets and keep warm?

questions.prompt: What point does he make about Alexander the Great and his mule driver?
options: Death brought them both to the same place
Both were punished by the gods
questions.explanation: Fame and power do not change what happens to everyone in the end.

questions.prompt: What does he tell himself in Book 10 about the good person?
options: To write a book about virtue
To look for a teacher of virtue
To stop talking about what a good person should be and simply be one
To wait until old age to decide
questions.explanation: The Meditations are exercises for acting, not theories.

questions.prompt: How does the book end?
options: Comparing death to an actor dismissed from the stage before the fifth act, and urging him to leave serenely
questions.explanation: Three acts can be a whole play; the one who dismisses you does so kindly.

books.title: The Last Days of Socrates
books.author: Plato

fieldNotes.law: a trial, and a man who obeys the law that kills him
fieldNotes.education: a teacher accused of corrupting the young
fieldNotes.humanities: the founding scene of philosophy

books.synopsis: Socrates is put on trial in Athens for impiety and corrupting the young, refuses to escape and spends his last day arguing that the soul does not die.

questions.prompt: Why is Euthyphro at the courthouse when he meets Socrates?
options: He is accused of impiety too
He is a juror in Socrates' trial
He is suing a neighbor over land
He is prosecuting his own father for the death of a laborer
questions.explanation: Socrates is amazed that he is so sure this is what piety requires.

questions.prompt: What is the famous question Socrates asks Euthyphro?
options: Is something pious because the gods love it, or do they love it because it is pious?
Is it ever right to lie?
questions.explanation: The dialogue ends without a definition: Euthyphro suddenly has somewhere else to be.

questions.prompt: What did the oracle at Delphi say about Socrates?
options: That no one was wiser than he was
That he was a danger to the city
questions.explanation: Socrates concludes that he is wiser only because he knows that he does not know.

questions.prompt: What does Socrates first propose as his 'penalty' after being found guilty?
options: Free meals at public expense, like a benefactor of the city
questions.explanation: He later offers a fine guaranteed by friends, Plato among them, but the jury votes for death.

questions.prompt: Which famous line does Socrates say in his defense?
options: The unexamined life is not worth living
Man is the measure of all things
questions.explanation: He would rather die than stop questioning people.

questions.prompt: What does Crito offer Socrates in prison?
options: To help him escape from Athens
To bring him poison so he can die early
questions.explanation: His friends have money ready and places he could go.

questions.prompt: How does Socrates explain his refusal?
options: He is too old to travel
He wants to become a martyr for the gods
He imagines the Laws of Athens telling him that escaping would wrong the city that raised him
questions.explanation: Doing wrong in return for wrong is never just.

questions.prompt: What does Socrates say a true philosopher is doing all his life?
questions.explanation: Philosophy separates the soul from the body as much as possible, which is what death completes.

questions.prompt: How is Socrates executed?
options: He is thrown from a cliff
He drinks a cup of hemlock
questions.explanation: He drinks it calmly while his friends weep.

questions.prompt: What are Socrates' last words?
options: That they owe a cock to Asclepius and must not forget to pay it
questions.explanation: Asclepius was the god of healing; many readers see death as a cure in the line.

books.title: The Symposium
books.author: Plato

fieldNotes.humanities: the oldest great conversation about love
fieldNotes.arts: love as the pursuit of beauty

books.synopsis: At a dinner party in Athens, a group of friends each give a speech in praise of love, until Socrates and a drunken Alcibiades turn the night upside down.

chapters.title: The party and the first speeches

questions.prompt: What is being celebrated at Agathon's house?
options: Agathon's victory with his first tragedy
A victory at the Olympic Games
questions.explanation: The guests are still tired from the previous day's drinking, so they agree to drink moderately.

questions.prompt: What do the guests decide to do instead of heavy drinking?
options: Listen to the flute girl all night
Each gives a speech in praise of Love (Eros)
questions.explanation: The idea comes from Phaedrus, through the doctor Eryximachus.

questions.prompt: What distinction does Pausanias make?
options: Between a heavenly love and a common, purely physical love
Between love for men and love for the gods
Between young love and old love
questions.explanation: He says there are two Aphrodites and therefore two kinds of Eros.

questions.prompt: What myth does Aristophanes tell about the origin of love?
options: Love was born from the sea foam
Love is a punishment for stealing fire
Humans were once double beings that Zeus split in two, and love is the search for our other half
Humans were made from clay by Prometheus
questions.explanation: The comic poet's story is one of the most famous explanations of love ever told.

questions.prompt: Why does Aristophanes speak later than planned?
options: He is late to the party
He refuses to speak before Socrates
questions.explanation: The doctor Eryximachus speaks in his place and prescribes a cure.

questions.prompt: Who taught Socrates about love, according to his speech?
options: Diotima, a wise woman from Mantinea
questions.explanation: Socrates presents his ideas as lessons he received from her.

questions.prompt: What is Love, according to Diotima?
options: The most beautiful of the gods
Neither a god nor a mortal but a spirit in between, always lacking and seeking
questions.explanation: Love is the child of Resource and Poverty, so it is always in need.

questions.prompt: Where does the 'ascent' of love lead in the end?
options: From one beautiful body to the vision of Beauty itself
questions.explanation: Each step moves on: bodies, souls, laws, knowledge and finally Beauty itself.

questions.prompt: What does Alcibiades compare Socrates to?
options: Statues of Silenus that look ugly outside but hold images of gods inside
A god disguised as a beggar
questions.explanation: Socrates' plain surface hides a rare inner beauty.

questions.prompt: What story does Alcibiades tell about Socrates?
options: How Socrates saved him in a shipwreck
How Socrates won a drinking contest at Delphi
How Socrates taught him to write poetry
How he tried to seduce Socrates and Socrates resisted
questions.explanation: He also praises Socrates' courage and endurance in the army.

questions.prompt: How does the night end?
options: At dawn Socrates is still talking, then goes off to spend the day as usual
questions.explanation: He has drunk as much as anyone and shows no sign of it.

books.title: Confessions
books.author: Saint Augustine

fieldNotes.humanities: the first great autobiography
fieldNotes.psychology: memory, time and a restless mind

books.synopsis: A North African bishop tells God, and us, the story of his restless youth, his ambitions and his conversion, and then asks what memory and time really are.

questions.prompt: What does Augustine say about the human heart at the very beginning?
options: It is ruled by the stars
It is restless until it rests in God
It can be known by reason alone
questions.explanation: This idea runs through the whole book.

questions.prompt: Why does the teenage Augustine steal pears with his friends?

books.title: The Psychology of Money
books.author: Morgan Housel

fieldNotes.business: saving, investing and risk explained without formulas
fieldNotes.psychology: why people make strange decisions with money

books.synopsis: In twenty short chapters, Morgan Housel argues that doing well with money depends more on behavior, patience and humility than on intelligence.

options: He died in a mountaineering accident before college
questions.explanation: Housel uses the two friends to show how luck and risk shape outcomes.

questions.prompt: Why does Rajat Gupta appear in the chapter 'Never Enough'?
options: He was rich and respected but risked everything for more with insider trading
He gave all his money away
He lost everything in a crash

questions.prompt: What does Housel point out about Warren Buffett's fortune?
options: He made it in one trade
Most of it came after his 65th birthday, thanks to compounding over time
He lost most of it in 2008

When you see someone in a nice car, you think about the car, not about admiring the driver
questions.explanation: People want respect, but possessions rarely earn it.

questions.prompt: What does Housel say is the highest dividend money can pay?

questions.prompt: What is the 'End of History Illusion' in the chapter 'You'll Change'?

options: Because setbacks happen quickly and loudly while progress happens slowly

questions.prompt: In 'Confessions,' what does Housel say his family did with their house?

questions.prompt: How long is the average human life, according to the title?

questions.explanation: Burkeman says it is absurdly short.

questions.prompt: How did medieval peasants experience time, according to Burkeman?

They felt always in a hurry
questions.explanation: Time was just the rhythm of tasks and seasons.
